127.title: [Demo Guide] Scaffold features and layers with one command (construct create)
127.body:
<!-- demo-curator:v1 -->
**Who it is for:** a developer adding a new feature to a Construct project.

**The problem it solves:** Creating the right folders and files in the right layers by hand is slow and easy to get subtly wrong; teammates end up with different structures.

![hero](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenewurbankid-web/construct/ui-screenshots/ui/e2e/screenshots/demos/5-ui-create-layer-result.png)

### Contents
| Sub-issue | User story | Benefit | Surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| #128 | As a developer I want to create a whole feature skeleton in one command | Every layer folder exists, correctly named, in 0.01s | CLI + UI |
| #129 | As a developer I want to create one correctly-placed, correctly-named file | No guessing the folder or naming convention (0.02s) | CLI + UI |
| #130 | As a developer I want to create several layers of one unit at once | A full vertical slice, 6 files in 0.04s, same result every time | CLI + UI |

### Why this matters
The structure Construct enforces is generated for you, not typed from memory.
Same command, same files, every time, on any machine.
Each step reports its own time, so you can see what it costs (fractions of a second).

**Evidence from a real run:** `create feature products` 0.01s; a six-layer slice 6 files in 0.04s total; two independent runs produced byte-identical output (`diff -r` clean).

*Verified on `main` @ `8dd69f5` (2026-09-18): commands re-run and screenshots re-shot against current main.* Style guide: `docs/DEMOS.md`. Part of #125.

---

Part of #125 (Demos module). First-ever ticket under that epic — this parent + its subtasks set the template every future demo ticket follows.

Parent/tracking ticket for demonstrating `construct create` (feature & layer scaffolding), on both the CLI and the Dashboard's Create form in the Cockpit UI. Split into one subtask per distinct thing `create` can scaffold, each independently closable:

- #128 — creating a new feature (`construct create feature` / `construct feature create`)
- #129 — creating a single file within a feature (`construct create <layer>` / `construct generate <layer>`)
- #130 — creating several files at once, a "vertical slice" (`construct create layer` / `construct generate layer`)

Each subtask is fully self-contained: a "Command line" section and a "Web UI" section that each stand on their own, with their own real example and real evidence (terminal transcript or screenshot) — no subtask depends on reading another subtask, and no section within a subtask depends on reading the other section, to get the complete picture of that capability.

This parent closes once all three subtasks are closed and verified.

> **As a** developer **I want** a new feature's folders created for me **so that** I do not hand-build the structure

### Benefit
- **Who benefits:** developers and reviewers.
- **Problem it removes:** hand-creating the layer folders (and getting names or places wrong).
- **Evidence:** `construct create feature products` created the feature in 0.01s with `[llm: 0 calls]`; the UI's Create form does the same in one click.

*Verified on `main` @ `8dd69f5` (2026-09-18): commands re-run and screenshots re-shot against current main.* The full CLI and UI walkthrough is in the write-up comment(s) below; where a comment predates this block, this block wins.

Part of #127 (Demos epic #125). Demonstrates: `construct create feature <name>`, its short form `construct feature create <name>`, and the "A new feature" option in the Dashboard's Create form.

## What this does today

Creates a brand-new feature: a folder with the seven standard sub-folders (controllers, workflows, hooks, domain, services, pages, components) plus a small `types.ts` and `index.ts`, ready for you to start filling in. It's the same result whichever surface you use — command line or the web UI — because the UI calls the exact same code the command line does.

## How to use it

### Command line

This section stands on its own — everything below was run for real, start to finish, from a terminal.

Long form:

```
$ node bin/construct.mjs create feature billing --dir /tmp/demo-project
Created feature billing at features/billing
[tool: scaffolded the file(s) above from templates] [llm: 0 calls — filling in the logic is a separate step, by you or whichever LLM you choose]
```

Short form (same result):

```
$ node bin/construct.mjs feature create payments --dir /tmp/demo-project
Created feature payments at features/payments
```

(Note: the short form prints just the "Created feature..." line — it skips the extra tool/LLM summary line the long form adds. Same files either way.)

145.title: [Demo Guide] Import a whole page by its URL: scan, plan, approve, build (guided route import)
145.body:
<!-- demo-curator:v1 -->
**Who it is for:** a team migrating a legacy page or route into Construct.

**The problem it solves:** Migrating a route by hand means finding every file it touches, deciding how to split them and writing the port, with no review point.

![hero](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenewurbankid-web/construct/ui-screenshots/ui/e2e/screenshots/demos/route-import-146-ui-1-plan-proposed.png)

### Contents
| Sub-issue | User story | Benefit | Surface |
|---|---|---|---|
| #146 | As a team lead I want the route scanned and a plan proposed that I must approve | Nothing is built until a human says yes; the scan is deterministic | CLI + UI |
| #147 | As a developer I want the approved plan built, with AI-written logic per file | 8 files ported in about 2 minutes with a local model, no network | CLI + UI |

### Why this matters
A human approves the plan before any file is written.
The scan and the scaffold are deterministic; only the per-file logic uses a model.
The per-file writing can run on a local model (Ollama), with no network call for that step.

**Evidence from a real run:** the UI run on 2026-09-18 wrote 8 files via local Ollama (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`) in 1.8 minutes end to end.

*Verified on `main` @ `8dd69f5` (2026-09-18): commands re-run and screenshots re-shot against current main.* Style guide: `docs/DEMOS.md`. Part of #125.

---

Part of #125 (Demos module).

## What this demonstrates
`construct import --route <path>` -- give it a real route (a URL like
/products, or the folder that owns its page.tsx) from an existing,
non-Construct app, and it brings that whole page/feature into a Construct
project through one guided flow. This is the flagship, recommended way to
import a real feature (as opposed to the simpler single-file `construct
import <name> --from <path>` already demoed in #134) -- positioning it as
the standard import flow per the user's request.

## The real pipeline (verify against current code before writing anything -- don't assume)
1. **Scan/trace** -- deterministic, AST-based (`route-resolver.mjs`,

- **Who benefits:** team leads and reviewers.
- **Problem it removes:** unreviewed bulk migrations.

Part of #145.

## What this demonstrates
Give `construct import --route <path>` a real route from an existing,
non-Construct app. It traces the route's real import graph deterministically
(AST-based, no AI), hands the full trace to one combined AI call that
proposes a Construct-shaped plan (which files become which layers), then
shows you that plan for approval before anything gets written.

Separate, independent CLI and UI sections, real terminal output from an
actual run (the `claude` CLI is installed and working in this environment
-- use it for real), real Playwright screenshots (frugal), plain language,
rule-12 closing structure. Verify against `src/route-resolver.mjs` and
`src/cli.mjs`'s `runImportRouteWizardEventDriven` before writing anything
-- confirm the scan step really is AST-only with no AI call, since that's
the whole point of this demo's accuracy.
